draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Raigad Fort! After his coronation in 1674, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj made this hilltop the capital of his Hindavi Swaraj. At 1,200 acres it's called the largest fort in Asia, sitting 820 metres up in the Sahyadris.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat up on the fort, so carry water and snacks for the climb and eat properly down near Mahad.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Meghadambari, the spot of Shivaji Maharaj's royal throne, is an 11 min walk, and Nagarkhana is the same distance. Takmak Tok is about 13 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet corner of the fort and take in the panoramic views over the Sahyadri range, it's worth the climb.
moodReplies.surprise-me: About 1,550 people once lived up here on the fort, in families of about five on average.

tips.title: Take the ropeway if the steps are too much.
tips.body: Walking up means about 1,737 steps, while the Raigad Ropeway gets you to the fort in about four minutes.

tips.title: Start the climb early.
tips.body: The fort sits 820 metres up and is spread over 1,200 acres, so give yourself plenty of daylight to walk around.

story.title: Rairee
story.body: The fort near Mahad was once known as Rairee or Rairy Fort. It's counted among the strongest fortresses on the Deccan Plateau.

story.title: Built for a king
story.body: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and his chief engineer Hiroji Indulkar oversaw the buildings and structures on the fort. About 1,550 people lived up here.

story.title: Capital of Swaraj
story.body: After his coronation as king in 1674, Shivaji Maharaj chose Raigad as the capital of his Hindavi Swaraj.

story.title: Steps or ropeway
story.body: Visitors climb about 1,737 steps or ride the 750 metre Raigad Ropeway. Either way, the views over the Sahyadris are the reward.
